title: Audio overview — July 8, 2026
description: A source-linked English audio overview of the day's proceedings.

segments.heading: Introduction
segments.text: This is Working Draft's audio overview of the Impeachment Trial of Vice President Sara Duterte for July 8, 2026. This is a working reference, not an official Senate record.

segments.heading: The big picture
segments.text: The July 8 session concluded the cross-examination and senator-judge questioning of National Bureau of Investigation Senior Agent John Mark Calilung. The record focused on revisions to the bureau's referral, the source and authentication of the recorded video, the scope of Calilung's investigation, and the context of the statements under review. Defense counsel read a February Department of Justice certification that had recommended further case buildup. Calilung testified that a later certification found the revised submission sufficient for preliminary investigation. He said his authentication relied on O-B-S screen-recording software and manual comparison, rather than an original-source recording or a forensic-tool analysis of this video. In its allotted response, the defense argued that the prosecution had not proved that Vice President Sara Duterte contracted an assassin, and that the statements did not constitute an impeachable high crime. The court allowed broad cross-examination, left admissibility questions for formal offer, and ordered written submissions and later oral argument on pending subpoena requests involving a sealed box and bank records. The court adjourned to July 13, when the prosecution said Jeremy Lotoc would be its next witness.

segments.heading: What happened
segments.text: Before cross-examination, Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero gave defense counsel Carlo Joaquin Narvasa the same five minutes and 18 seconds previously used by prosecution counsel for an Article Four argument. The response would be delivered after cross-examination. Pia Cayetano withdrew her earlier motion to strike the prosecution argument in the interest of equal treatment.

segments.heading: What happened
segments.text: Narvasa's cross-examination challenged Calilung's training, the source of his photo-and-video authentication instruction, the completeness of the National Bureau of Investigation's papers, and the accuracy of his transcript of the November 23 recording.

segments.heading: What happened
segments.text: The defense confronted Calilung with a February 5 Department of Justice certification recommending further case buildup because the referral lacked evidence needed to prove the crimes' elements. Calilung later testified that the bureau complied with the listed requirements and received a second certification saying the evidence was sufficient for preliminary investigation.

segments.heading: The court's directions
segments.text: The chair limited the use of the training provider's partnership materials to showing what Calilung had read or seen. It instructed senator-judges that he was not competent to establish the truth of those documents' contents.

segments.heading: The court's directions
segments.text: The chair conditionally allowed cross-examination using documents that had not been introduced through the prosecution's direct examination, provided the defense connected them to testing Calilung's credibility, accuracy, or completeness.

segments.heading: The court's directions
segments.text: The court overruled the prosecution's relevance objection to questions about differences in Calilung's transcript. It held that the defense could use them on cross-examination to test his accuracy and truthfulness.

segments.heading: The prosecution's position
segments.text: The prosecution objected to the defense's use of the training provider's partnership documents and website. It later challenged documents used on cross-examination without marking or source identification. The chair preserved those objections while allowing limited or conditional use.

segments.heading: The prosecution's position
segments.text: In response to Bam Aquino, prosecution counsel said witnesses other than Calilung would address the alleged hitman; Calilung had been presented only for the video investigation.

segments.heading: The prosecution's position
segments.text: The prosecution elected not to conduct redirect examination of Calilung and later said Jeremy Lotoc would be presented at the next hearing rather than on July 8.

segments.heading: The defense's position
segments.text: Through cross-examination, the defense used the training provider's partnership papers and website to question the foundation of Calilung's photo-and-video authentication training. The court permitted the documents only to establish what Calilung had seen, not the truth of their contents.

segments.heading: The defense's position
segments.text: The defense used the February 5 DOJ certification to argue that the first NBI referral was incomplete, emphasizing absent recorder and transcript affidavits, missing or unclear electronic media, lack of individual journalist affidavits, and nonparticipation by the alleged offended parties.

segments.heading: The defense's position
segments.text: Narvasa stressed that the NBI initiated and filed the complaint, the DOJ directed the investigation and would assess prosecution, and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. headed the executive branch while being an alleged offended party. This was a defense characterization of the institutional relationship, not a court finding of improper influence.

segments.heading: Witnesses and evidence
segments.text: During cross-examination, defense counsel read a February 5 Department of Justice certification that recommended returning the referral for further case buildup and listed seven deficiencies. The items included missing affidavits from recorders and transcript makers, missing or unclear video media, no individual affidavits from interviewed journalists, and no participation by the alleged offended parties.

segments.heading: Witnesses and evidence
segments.text: Calilung testified that the revised National Bureau of Investigation submission complied with the Department of Justice's requirements and later received a certification that its evidence was sufficient for preliminary investigation. That described a threshold prosecutorial assessment, not a criminal conviction or a finding by the impeachment court.

segments.heading: Witnesses and evidence
segments.text: Calilung said the NBI began the investigation without a private complainant. He also said he had no personal knowledge whether the President, First Lady, or former House Speaker filed complaints, and the chair confirmed that affidavits from the two journalists discussed on cross were not attached to the February 10 affidavit.

segments.heading: What remains unresolved
segments.text: The admissibility and weight of the February DOJ certifications, revised NBI affidavit, and other materials first used to confront Calilung on cross-examination remained undecided because the documents had not yet been formally offered.

segments.heading: What remains unresolved
segments.text: The alleged hitman's existence and any related evidence remained outside Calilung's assigned investigation; prosecution counsel said another witness or witnesses would address that subject.

segments.heading: What remains unresolved
segments.text: The court had not decided the prosecution's subpoena request concerning a sealed box returned to its originating agency, or the related bank-record subpoena issue. Both matters were set for written memoranda and oral argument on Wednesday before a ruling.

segments.heading: How to use this overview
segments.text: The episode page links every substantive point to the timed transcript and the original Senate video. Verify consequential wording against those sources before publication.
